svg.aria-label: AI features view of Dependinator: the features that ask an AI (cycle and rule reviews, Suggest rules, the Ask panel, About Node, Improve Comments, the codebase tour, line labels) build a prompt and a JSON schema and go through the UI's IAiService, which knows the providers and the user's default. The Claude API route and the Claude Code route are behind the IClaudeService RPC interface, implemented by Dependinator.Claude in the language server or the dev host; the Copilot route is behind IVsCodeModelService, which the language server forwards to the VS Code extension and its language models; the AI chat route is copy and paste. In the other direction, the MCP server in Dependinator.Mcp gives AI agents, Claude Code runs and the app's own tool loops nine read-only tools, which ask the open diagram through the IModelQueryService RPC interface that the UI's ModelQueries answers.

What the app keeps to itself
· prompts: one builder per feature, with shared
· checks: suggested rules are checked again,
tour stops must be nodes, names become links
· decisions: nothing is accepted, allowed or
added to the model until the user says so

and dependencies, paths, cycles, rules, a check

the key: VS Code secrets or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

"Use your AI chat": the user copies the prompt and pastes the answer back

Solid blue: a feature asks an AI; every route gets the same prompt and returns the same JSON answer, so a feature does not know which AI answered. Dashed brown: an AI looks things up in the open model.
The [Rpc] calls are plain calls in the dev host and cross the JSON-RPC tunnel in VS Code (view 5). The standalone browser app has only the AI chat route.
Language server (VS Code) or dev host
never in the browser app, which has no key and no files
